This is my sorghum plot, and the rains here in the North East come only once a year, so I must make it count. I have some schooling and I own this land, so I will put fertilizer — maybe one bag of NPK and some urea when the sorghum is knee-high. I also carry manure from my animals to the field before planting, because fertilizer alone is costly. For seed I will use what I saved from last harvest, like my father did; the improved sorghum seed is not easy to find at the agro-dealer here, and my local variety handles the dry spells well. My wife and children help me, but with 1.28 ha and weeding twice, I will call two or three young men for a few days during weeding and harvest.
